packageRules.description: Majors wait for approval on the Dependency Dashboard instead of opening PRs.
PiPulse's own image in compose.yaml follows :latest; the release stamps the shipped file with its tag, so a digest pin only goes stale.
The workflows and their containers run the Node that ships on the Pi (armhf stays on 22).
Types for the oldest supported Node (engines >=22.13), so nothing newer than Node 22 typechecks.
Only updates that change what ships make a release: runtime dependencies (bundled into the app or the dashboard).
The Node bundled into every native install.
The Docker image's base (Node and Debian in the image).

GitHub Actions version updates wait 3 days after the new version's commit date, like npm. A digest-only update (a floating tag such as v7 moved to a new commit) ages against the matched version's original date, so this does not hold a force-pushed tag (github-tags has no push date); the digest rule below covers that.

A digest-only Actions update (a floating tag such as v7 pointed at a new commit) is how a hijacked tag reaches a workflow, and the age gate cannot see it, so a person merges these. About one a month so far.

Every npm update waits 3 days after its release, dev dependencies included: they run in CI and build the dashboard, and most compromised releases are pulled within days. Docker digests carry no release date, so they are not gated.
